title: Choosing program marks
subject: A better way to pick favorite marks, order them, and send the choice, on the program mark ideas page

brief.background: The program mark ideas page sets hundreds of candidate marks for Organization, Content and Discovery side by side, but a pick lives only in the open tab: there is no way to keep favorites, see them together in an order, or send them back. The owner wants to mark favorites, see them at the top, drag them into order, and submit. Afterward the owner should be able to say which marks lead for each program, and a session should be able to read the same list.
brief.methodology: The eight concepts were sketched before any was judged. Each had to say how a favorite is marked while scanning a long pile on a phone, where favorites gather, how their order is set, and how the choice gets back to a session: the estate's pick calls already record answers beside the call and comment on its pull request.

ideas.title: Star and shortlist
ideas.commentary:
Photo culling's flag: a star on every tile, and the starred marks gather in a **Favorites** row at the top of the program's column, numbered, in an order you drag.

Marking stays one tap while scanning, and ordering happens only among the few you kept. The first favorite is the pick the lineup shows.

ideas.title: Ranked slots
ideas.commentary:
A ranked-choice ballot: three numbered slots per program, and a tap drops a mark into the next free slot.

The order is explicit from the start, but three slots cap the shortlist, and changing your mind means emptying a slot first.

ideas.title: Pairwise duel
ideas.commentary:
Two marks at a time, and a tap picks the better; the order is computed from the duels.

Good at settling close calls, but the pairs grow fast: eight favorites make 28 duels, so it only suits a shortlist that already exists.

ideas.title: Swipe deck
ideas.commentary:
One mark at a time, large, swiped to keep or skip, then the kept ones ordered.

Each mark gets full attention, but hundreds of references make a long deck, and the side-by-side comparison the page is for disappears.

ideas.title: Love, maybe, no
ideas.commentary:
Three lanes per program, and marks dragged between them; the order inside **Love** is the ranking.

It keeps a middle tier, but dragging out of a pile of hundreds is slow, and lanes take width a phone does not have.

ideas.title: Lineup composer
ideas.commentary:
The lineup beside the repository marks becomes the editor: each program's favorites stack under its slot, and the one on top is in the lineup.

It judges a mark where it will live, next to the others, which is the page's real test; it needs a favorites list to stack from.

ideas.title: Favorites sheet
ideas.commentary:
A shopping cart: stars anywhere, and a bottom sheet holds every program's favorites in rows, with drag to order and **Send** inside.

One place for the whole answer, but the sheet covers the pile while it is open.

ideas.commentary:
Favorites become rows in the estate's Lists view, ordered there, and the ideas page only stars.

Durable and editable anywhere, but the choosing splits across two places, and the comparison by eye stays on the ideas page.

grafts: the rank numbers on the favorites, with the first marked as the pick
the first favorite of each program fills its place in the lineup
a send bar that names each program's favorites and holds Send
selection.rationale: Starring keeps the scan fast on a long pile, and ordering only the kept few keeps dragging cheap on a phone. Putting the favorites in each column's sticky block keeps them beside the ideas they came from, and the lineup shows the leaders in place. Send uses the pick call the estate already answers.
